rows.subtype: Being the subject of office talk [Receiver]
rows.description: An employee finds out that colleagues speculate about their personal life or promotion. They feel exposed and may over-manage their image, wasting energy on impressions.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: An adult with a concern about someone speaks to them directly and privately, not to third parties. Directness is harder in the moment but prevents the slow poison of talk behind the back.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: Young children begin declaring that someone cannot play or is their best friend. Early exclusion tests power and closeness, and adults can gently teach that everyone gets a turn.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A group of children names itself, makes rules and decides who is in. The thrill of being chosen is real, and it depends on someone else being left out.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child watches the popular group laughing and feels a sharp mix of longing and hurt. They may try harder to be noticed or pretend not to care.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, nostalgia, hurt

rows.description: A child or teacher invites a lone child into a game without fuss. A small, ordinary act of inclusion changes a school day for the one included.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager judges their standing by who sits with them, who tags them and what they wear. They may drop old friends who lower their status and feel a private ache about it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager is not openly bullied but is never invited, tagged or waited for. Being ignored gradually convinces them that something is wrong with them personally.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A peer watches the group's leader decide who is in favour this week, keeping everyone anxious and obedient. Fear of losing standing keeps the members loyal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Hierarchies by college, city and money [Observer]
rows.description: A student sees the pecking order shift to college brand, English fluency, wealth and connections. Status markers are less obvious than in school but no less sorted.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
